problem:
Problem Statement
Problem: Graph Theory - 12
Let G be a 2-connected plane graph. Prove that G is bipartite if and only if the boundary
of every face of G is an even cycle.
1
proof_numbered:
0001 | Solution:
0002 | We shall prove the statement in two parts: first showing that if G is bipartite,
0003 | then the boundary of every face is an even cycle, and then proving the converse.
0004 | Definitions and Preliminaries - A **2-connected graph** is a connected graph with no
0005 | cut vertices. - A **plane graph** is a graph embedded in the plane without edge crossings.
0006 | - A **face** of a plane graph is a maximal connected region of the complement of the graph
0007 | in the plane. - The **boundary** of a face is the subgraph formed by the edges and vertices
0008 | adjacent to the face. - A graph is **bipartite** if its vertices can be partitioned into two
0009 | sets such that no two vertices within the same set are adjacent.
0010 | Part 1: If G is bipartite, then the boundary of every face is an even cycle.
0011 | **Proof:** Assume G is bipartite with bipartition (A, B). Consider any face F of G.
0012 | The boundary of F is a cycle (since G is 2-connected, the boundary cannot be a forest or
0013 | have cut vertices).
0014 | Let C be the boundary cycle of F with vertices v1, v2, . . . , vk, v1 in order. Since G is
0015 | bipartite, the vertices alternate between A and B as we traverse C. Without loss of generality,
0016 | suppose v1 ∈A. Then: - v2 ∈B, - v3 ∈A, - . . . , - vk ∈B if k is even, or vk ∈A if k is odd.
0017 | But vk is adjacent to v1 ∈A, so vk must be in B. Therefore, k must be even. Hence, the
0018 | boundary cycle C has an even number of edges, i.e., it is an even cycle.
0019 | Part 2: If the boundary of every face is an even cycle, then G is bipartite.
0020 | **Proof:** Assume that the boundary of every face of G is an even cycle. We shall show
0021 | that G is bipartite by constructing a bipartition.
0022 | Since G is 2-connected, it admits an **ear decomposition**: we can construct G by
0023 | starting with a cycle and iteratively adding paths (ears) between existing vertices.
0024 | 1. **Base Case:** Start with any face F of G. Its boundary is an even cycle C. An even
0025 | cycle is bipartite, so we can properly 2-color its vertices with colors, say, red and blue.
0026 | 2. **Inductive Step:** Suppose we have a subgraph H of G that is bipartite with a
0027 | proper 2-coloring. Add an ear P (a path) to H to form a larger subgraph H′. The endpoints
0028 | of P lie in H and are colored, say, red and blue (since H is bipartite).
0029 | - If the length of P is odd, the other endpoint would receive the same color as the starting
0030 | point, leading to a monochromatic edge when P is added. But this cannot happen because
0031 | the boundary of the new face created by adding P must be an even cycle. The new face’s
0032 | boundary consists of P and a path in H between the endpoints of P. The sum of the lengths
0033 | of these two paths must be even (to form an even cycle), so P must have even length if the
0034 | path in H has even length, and odd length if the path in H has odd length. However, since
0035 | H is bipartite, any path between two vertices of the same color has even length, and between
0036 | different colors has odd length. Thus, the parity of P must match appropriately to ensure
0037 | the new face boundary is even, and the coloring can be extended consistently.
0038 | Therefore, we can always extend the proper 2-coloring to H′ by alternating colors along
0039 | P.
0040 | By induction, the entire graph G can be properly 2-colored, hence it is bipartite.
0041 | Conclusion We have shown both directions: - If G is bipartite, then every face boundary
0042 | is an even cycle. - If every face boundary is an even cycle, then G is bipartite.
0043 | Thus, the statement is proved.
0044 | G is bipartite if and only if the boundary of every face of G is an even cycle.
0045 | 1
